widgets_values:
## One opening anchor → 15.08-second ottoman-focused travel

The loader uses `krea2_anypaint_00001_.png` as the exact first frame. Loop closure is disabled: only the opening is image-anchored, and the final west-side viewpoint is free. The FL2VA checkpoint supports this I2VA route. Output remains **362 frames at 24 fps = 15.08 seconds**.

The prompt contains no numbered `[Shot]` tags and no cuts. The camera moves **clockwise only** through a 270-degree arc. It never reverses, jumps behind the easel, or returns to the first frame. The opening is the farthest point; radius shrinks progressively from 3.20 to 2.00 meters as the camera approaches the back of the easel, then stays close through the final west-side view. Height changes gently from 1.50 down to 1.12, up to 1.55, and back to 1.20 meters.

The path geometry is centered on the floor midpoint between the ottoman and easel, but the **white ottoman is the primary optically tracked subject**. The complete easel and blank paper remain visible as the secondary subject, growing closer through parallax rather than becoming the orbit center. The right wall stays plain neutral off-white, with a closed white double sliding entry and wooden coat rack.

Twelve five-frame checkpoint windows match the 270-degree decoder plan. Every frame remains a potential cinematic capture, and full-frame saving stays enabled for manual selection.

nodes.title: Exact 15.08-second ottoman-focused inward travel · no [Shot] tags
widgets_values:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from Shot 1) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: One uninterrupted live-action cinematic architectural camera take begins from the exact pixels, composition, perspective, exposure, materials, lighting, and room geometry of <Picture 1>. This is a first-frame-anchored travel with a free final viewpoint. There is no final-frame reference and no requirement to return to the opening camera.

Preserve one small sparse drawing studio as a rigid three-dimensional set. The tall dark-brown easel keeps its completely blank white paper, the single seat remains immediately behind it, and the low white cube ottoman remains fixed on the white shag rug. The right/east wall is always plain smooth neutral off-white and never inherits the gray-green color or board from the left/west wall. The right-side entry is a closed plain white double sliding door with two equal panels, beside a simple bare wooden coat rack. Trees are visible outside the windows, with their number and placement left to the scene. Do not add studio furniture, art supplies, artworks, or clutter. The room, objects, lighting, and shadows remain fixed; only the physical camera moves.

The white ottoman is the primary tracked visual subject for the entire take. Keep its complete silhouette, top, side faces, rug contact, and upholstery construction clear. The complete easel and blank paper are a mandatory secondary subject that remains visible in the same frame, but the camera never tracks or orbits around the easel. Define camera-path center C as the floor point exactly halfway between the ottoman center and the midpoint of the easel's front feet. The path curves around C, while the optical axis continuously tracks a point 0.65 meters above the ottoman center. This makes the ottoman the compositional focus and causes the easel to change side and distance through parallax. Use the fixed source-matched rectilinear lens, approximately 32 mm full-frame equivalent, with no optical zoom and zero roll.

Follow one continuous 270-degree clockwise arc from the opening view toward camera-right. Never move counterclockwise, reverse direction, teleport, cut, dissolve, or jump behind the easel. Keep the simple smooth angular progression that worked in the earlier room coverage, but gradually shrink the radius from C so the arc becomes an inward spiral rather than a constant-radius circle. The opening camera is the farthest point of the entire take. Each later viewpoint is closer, and when the camera reaches the back and side of the easel it is at its closest range. Gently lower the camera during the first third, then raise it while approaching the easel, then descend slightly toward the free final view. These are small continuous pedestal changes inside the same clockwise move, never abrupt vertical jumps.

Every one of the 362 frames is a potential cinematic capture, not only the 12 named checkpoints. Keep the ottoman and easel visible together throughout, using the ottoman as foreground or midground focus and the easel as a strong secondary vertical. Use rug and floorboard leading lines, foreground-to-background separation, controlled parallax, balanced negative space, and restrained low or elevated angles. Maintain sharp focus, stable exposure, short-exposure clarity, coherent walls, and resolved object geometry in all intermediate frames. The five-frame checkpoint holds are gentle settles inside the same travel; motion resumes in the same clockwise direction after every hold.

At 00:00.000, Capture 1 begins at the exact source camera, 0.000 degrees on the clockwise path, approximately 3.20 meters from C and 1.50 meters high. This is the farthest view. Preserve the opening composition while establishing the ottoman as the tracked subject and retaining the easel, blank paper, seat, rug, windows, and double sliding entry. Hold from 00:00.000 through 00:00.083.

At 00:01.375, Capture 2 reaches 24.545 degrees clockwise, 3.00 meters from C and 1.42 meters high. Continue smoothly to camera-right with no reversal. Keep the complete ottoman prominent over the rug and the complete easel in the midground. Hold from 00:01.292 through 00:01.458.

At 00:02.750, Capture 3 reaches 49.091 degrees clockwise, 2.80 meters from C and 1.32 meters high. Continue the same inward clockwise arc. Use a cinematic front-right three-quarter view of the ottoman with the easel offset behind it; retain the plain east wall, double sliding entry, and coat rack. Hold from 00:02.667 through 00:02.833.

At 00:04.083, Capture 4 reaches 73.636 degrees clockwise, 2.60 meters from C and 1.20 meters high. The camera is now lower and closer on the east side. Track the ottoman, not the easel, while keeping the complete easel and seat separated by parallax. The east wall remains neutral off-white. Hold from 00:04.000 through 00:04.167.

At 00:05.458, Capture 5 reaches 98.182 degrees clockwise, 2.45 meters from C and 1.12 meters high, the lowest point of the travel. Continue past the east profile without stopping or changing direction. Frame the ottoman's side and top clearly with the entire easel beyond it and the double sliding entry as an architectural cue. Hold from 00:05.375 through 00:05.542.

At 00:06.833, Capture 6 reaches 122.727 degrees clockwise, 2.30 meters from C and 1.25 meters high. The camera begins a gentle rise while continuing inward toward the back-right side of the easel. The ottoman remains the focus; the easel shifts toward frame left and grows larger because the camera is physically approaching it. Hold from 00:06.750 through 00:06.917.

At 00:08.208, Capture 7 reaches 147.273 degrees clockwise, 2.15 meters from C and 1.42 meters high. Continue the same clockwise motion close to the easel's back-right quarter. Keep clear physical clearance but bring the camera substantially nearer to the easel than at the opening. Use parallax to expose the ottoman's rear-facing side and top while the complete easel remains at frame left. Hold from 00:08.125 through 00:08.292.

At 00:09.583, Capture 8 reaches 171.818 degrees clockwise, 2.00 meters from C and 1.55 meters high. This is the closest approach to the easel and the high point of the path, just to the right of the direct reverse axis so the easel cannot block the ottoman. Track the complete ottoman's back side as the primary subject; keep the complete easel and blank paper clearly visible in the left third, close enough for its rear construction to read. Hold from 00:09.500 through 00:09.667.

At 00:10.958, Capture 9 reaches 196.364 degrees clockwise, 2.00 meters from C and 1.50 meters high. Pass continuously behind the two-object relationship into the back-left quarter without a jump. The ottoman's back and opposite side remain prominent while the complete easel crosses smoothly toward frame right. Retain the south windows and trees as background depth. Hold from 00:10.875 through 00:11.042.

At 00:12.292, Capture 10 reaches 220.909 degrees clockwise, 2.05 meters from C and 1.38 meters high. Continue clockwise into a close northwest three-quarter view. Keep the ottoman as the tracked focus, the complete easel as the secondary vertical, most of the rug visible, and the gray-green board confined to the west wall. Hold from 00:12.208 through 00:12.375.

At 00:13.667, Capture 11 reaches 245.455 degrees clockwise, 2.10 meters from C and 1.28 meters high. Continue the same direction into a west-northwest side view. The camera remains much closer than the opening frame; show both complete objects with strong side parallax and clear rug contact. Hold from 00:13.583 through 00:13.750.

At 00:15.042, Capture 12 reaches 270.000 degrees clockwise, approximately 2.15 meters from C and 1.20 meters high. Finish naturally on the west side with no attempt to return to <Picture 1>. The ottoman remains the primary subject, the full easel and blank paper remain visible as the secondary subject, and the final composition is a resolved cinematic side angle of the pair. Hold this final resolved viewpoint through the last frame.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is one coherent photorealistic reconstruction of the same compact institutional art studio observed across <Picture 1> through <Picture 5>. <Picture 1> supplies the broad open-floor geometry, long frosted-window wall, gray wall board, and central dark wooden easel. <Picture 2> supplies the cream cube ottoman, cream shag-rug footprint, pale-green curtain corner, and near-easel relationships. <Picture 3> supplies the double doors, transom and window arrangement, stacked dark wooden easels, and clear floor aisle. <Picture 4> supplies the honey-brown coat stand, sketch-board construction, and close easel details. <Picture 5> supplies the cube-to-rug contact, easel legs and board, white hanging coat, and local object scale. Treat these pictures as equal complementary survey evidence of one room, not as separate rooms, source frames, timeline keyframes, or compositions to copy.
<Subject 2> is the exact central working zone inside <Subject 1>: the cream cube fixed on the cream shag rug together with the nearest upright dark wooden easel. Its coverage center C is the center of the cube's floor footprint. The cube, rug, and easel retain one fixed position and orientation relative to the windows, doors, wall board, floorboards, stacked easels, curtain, and coat stand.

summary:
[reference generation] Reconstruct <Subject 1> from the five semantic survey pictures, freeze the completed room, then photograph <Subject 2> from eight explicitly located static cameras separated by instantaneous hard cuts. Every viewpoint remains close to the working zone and uses a normal lens; there are no distant establishing images or loosely chosen angles.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in every shot): fully_preserved - retain one rectangular room, its dimensions, wall order, openings, fixtures, floorboard direction, furniture, materials, neutral exposure, soft frosted-window daylight, shadows, and all object relationships without drift or redesign across cuts.
<Subject 2> (appears in every shot): fully_preserved - retain the exact cream cube dimensions, two-part upholstery construction, horizontal seam, rounded piping, top-center seam, rug contact, rug footprint, and the nearby dark easel's construction, wear, orientation, and floor contacts. Only camera position, height, optical axis, lens, and framing may change.

detailed_description:
The target uses high-fidelity live-action architectural photography with realistic perspective, neutral white balance, crisp natural detail, controlled frosted-window highlights, soft daylight, clean shadow detail, and physically plausible materials. Reconcile the five pictures into one fixed coordinate system before the first frame. Define the long frosted-window wall as north; define the wall with the double doors and stacked easels as east; define the gray-board side and broad open wooden floor as south; define the pale-green-curtain and honey-brown-coat-stand corner as west. The cream rug and cube occupy the central working zone, with the nearest upright dark easel immediately adjacent. If a source crop hides a connection, infer only the shortest conservative continuation consistent with overlapping doors, windows, floorboards, rug edges, easels, and wall corners.

Across the complete 10.125-second target, the room behaves as a rigid surveyed set. The cube never spins, slides, scales, changes seams, or changes upholstery. The rug never moves or changes shape. The central easel, stacked easels, boards, stool, coat stand, hanging white coat, curtain, doors, windows, wall board, ceiling fixtures, floorboards, reflections, light sources, and shadows never move, multiply, disappear, or switch walls. Every cut is instantaneous: the first frame following a cut is already the fully resolved new camera. Do not render an orbit, travel frame, pan, dolly, truck, zoom, whip-pan, blur, dissolve, morph, or transitional viewpoint. Camera roll is 0 degrees in every shot, vertical wall edges stay vertical, exposure and white balance remain locked, and focus stays on C. No camera may be farther than 2.4 meters from C; use no lens wider than 45 mm. Avoid remote room-wide framing, empty-floor-dominated compositions, ceiling-dominated compositions, isolated product shots, macro crops, arbitrary corners, or invented camera positions. In every shot, <Subject 2> occupies roughly 50 to 70 percent of the frame and at least two named room anchors prove the camera's exact side of the room.

At 00:00.000, Camera A is due south of C on the clear open wooden floor, 2.4 meters from C and 1.45 meters above the floor. Use a 50 mm rectilinear lens, aim due north at the cube center with a 4-degree downward pitch and zero roll, and hold a static eye-level medium-wide composition. Place the cream cube and rug in the lower center, the nearest dark easel rising through the middle, the long frosted-window wall across the background, and a narrow edge of the gray wall board at frame left. Keep the cube fully visible, show its floor contact and complete top, and prevent empty floor from occupying more than the lower quarter. Extraction capture 1 is centered at 00:00.000; hold this exact camera and framing motionless from 00:00.000 through 00:00.083.

At 00:00.625, cut instantly to Camera B southwest of C, positioned where the gray-board side meets the open floor, 2.2 meters from C and 1.30 meters high. Use a 55 mm rectilinear lens, yaw northeast directly toward C, pitch down 3 degrees, and keep zero roll. Frame a close contextual three-quarter view: the cube remains complete in the lower-right-middle, the rug boundary and floorboards establish depth, the central easel is seen from its left-front quarter, and both the gray-board edge and at least one frosted opening remain visible. Do not back away into a wide room view. Extraction capture 2 is centered at 00:01.250; hold motionless from 00:01.167 through 00:01.333.

At 00:01.875, cut instantly to Camera C on the west side of C in the clear strip beside the pale-green-curtain and coat-stand corner, 2.0 meters from C and 1.15 meters high. Use a 50 mm lens, aim due east at C with a 2-degree downward pitch and zero roll. Make a contextual side view in which the cube is fully visible at center, the easel legs overlap the rug in physically correct depth, a controlled sliver of curtain or coat stand appears at frame left, and the double-door or stacked-easel wall is visible behind the working zone. The foreground anchor may border the frame but may not block the cube. Extraction capture 3 is centered at 00:02.500; hold motionless from 00:02.417 through 00:02.583.

At 00:03.167, cut instantly to Camera D northwest of C, just inside the room near the left end of the frosted-window wall but never outside or inside an object, 1.9 meters from C and 0.75 meters high. Use a 45 mm rectilinear lens, yaw southeast toward C, pitch upward 4 degrees, and keep zero roll. This is the only low camera: show the rug fibers and cube floor contact prominently, keep the complete cube silhouette, let the central easel rise behind it, and retain one frosted window frame plus the open-floor/gray-board side as background anchors. Do not exaggerate the low angle or distort verticals. Extraction capture 4 is centered at 00:03.792; hold motionless from 00:03.708 through 00:03.875.

At 00:04.417, cut instantly to Camera E due north of C in the clear interior strip in front of the frosted-window wall, 2.1 meters from C and 1.50 meters high. Use a 60 mm rectilinear lens, aim due south at C with a 5-degree downward pitch and zero roll. Create a reverse medium composition: the cube and its top seam remain complete, the back construction of the nearest easel is readable, and the open wooden floor and gray wall board establish the reverse direction. A narrow window-frame edge may remain at one border, but bright glazing must not dominate or clip the target. Extraction capture 5 is centered at 00:05.042; hold motionless from 00:04.958 through 00:05.125.

At 00:05.667, cut instantly to Camera F northeast of C, on the room side of the double doors and outside their swing path, 2.2 meters from C and 1.65 meters high. Use a 55 mm lens, yaw southwest precisely toward C, pitch down 8 degrees, and keep zero roll. Form a restrained high three-quarter view that reveals the cube's top-center seam, its horizontal side seam, the surrounding rug footprint, and the central easel's fixed relationship to it. Include a double-door jamb and part of the stacked-easel group as two discrete location anchors. The camera must remain near the area; do not turn this into a ceiling or room overview. Extraction capture 6 is centered at 00:06.292; hold motionless from 00:06.208 through 00:06.375.

At 00:06.917, cut instantly to Camera G due east of C in the clear aisle immediately in front of, but not inside, the stacked-easel storage zone, 1.8 meters from C and 1.10 meters high. Use a 65 mm rectilinear lens, aim due west at C with a 2-degree downward pitch and zero roll. Produce the tightest contextual profile: the complete cube occupies the central half of the image, the near easel's lower construction and floor contacts remain visible, the rug edge crosses the lower frame, and the curtain or coat-stand corner remains recognizable in the far background. Stacked easel rails may create a narrow foreground edge but may not obscure the target. Extraction capture 7 is centered at 00:07.583; hold motionless from 00:07.500 through 00:07.667.

At 00:08.208, cut instantly to Camera H southeast of C, on the open-floor side beside the double-door zone, 2.1 meters from C and 1.40 meters high. Use a 50 mm rectilinear lens, yaw northwest directly toward C, pitch down 4 degrees, and keep zero roll. Finish with a precise contextual three-quarter composition rather than a generic hero shot: keep the complete cube and most of the rug visible, show the nearest dark easel as the dominant vertical anchor, and retain both a frosted-window segment and the honey-brown coat stand or white hanging coat as distant orientation anchors. Match the scale and neutral exposure of the preceding shots. Extraction capture 8 is centered at 00:08.833; hold motionless from 00:08.750 through 00:08.917 and then keep this identical resolved frame static through 00:10.125.
